label: Corpus census bounds the strict-prefix surface: 57 manual-testing-playbook trees hold 2,682 scenario files and 1,012 ### Expected blocks across 990 files, but only 13 blocks contain a fenced literal transcript and only 26 contain an ellipsis anywhere; producer-line anchoring can fire on <=13 blocks (~1.3% of Expected blocks), so the F3 prefix rule's false-positive blast radius is bounded and its single known firing is a true positive (the live literal-naming case).

Live drift case: the literal-naming scenario's Expected line (line 90, ending 'Provide --phase-names with literal slugs.') is a strict prefix, without ellipsis, of the same document's own Evidence emission (line 119) and of the producer string at create.sh:1637 ('...literal slugs describing the concrete work.'), so the F3 EXPECTED_TRUNCATED class fires on current in-tree state without authoring a fixture.

The recorded --phase-count drift is remediated and cannot serve as live evidence: spec 018 records the silent catch-all path (spec.md:59) and the two corrected documents (spec.md:85-86), rg over .skilled/skills finds zero occurrences today, and create.sh now exits 1 on unknown options (create.sh:350); the scenario-option check would still have caught the doc side statically, so the case is a replay fixture.

Catalog anchor census: of 658 feature-catalog markdown files, 262 contain a .skilled/ path but only 6 carry path:line(-range) anchors, so retaining the parsed range at validate_catalog_package.py:593 changes behavior on 6 files while the path-existence half reaches up to 262; the sampled canonical-first-spec-root-resolution.md:47-48 citations resolve cleanly against spec-root-canonical-resolver.ts:12 and :43, so the check would pass the sample.

Catalog validator checks inherit no CI enforcement: run-script-tests.sh only globs test_*.py in its own directory (lines 7-12), the catalog fixture test sits at sk-create-feature-catalog/scripts/tests/test_validator_fixtures.py, and no workflow references the catalog validator or that test; the playbook validator is run fleet-wide with --strict (playbook-operator-contract.yml:61), so new playbook checks inherit enforcement and new catalog checks inherit none until the fixture test is wired to a runner.
